title: A smooth source with locally constant coefficients
statement:
Let $S$ be integral and of finite type over a field $k$, let
$\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(k)$, let $f:X\to S$ be a
separated smooth morphism of
finite type, and let $L$ be a finite locally constant
$\mathbf F_\ell$-sheaf. There is a nonempty open $U\subset S$
such that $Rf_{U,*}L|_{X_U}$ is bounded with finite locally
constant cohomology, and for every $v:T\to U$ with Noetherian $T$ the ordinary
base-change morphism

$$
v^*Rf_{U,*}L|_{X_U}\longrightarrow Rf_{T,*}L|_{X_T}
$$

is an isomorphism.
The notation refers to ordinary derived categories.

proof.text: Set $\lambda=\mathbf F_\ell$ and use only the ordinary small etale categories with this constant coefficient ring. The schemes $S$ and $X$ are Noetherian: a field is Noetherian, and [pqf-lem-locnoeth-lft] applies first to $S\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ and then to $X\to S$; finite type also gives quasi-compactness. The dimension function on $X$ is locally constant by [sbc-lem-smooth-relative-dimension-locally-constant] (Stacks Tag 02G1). Its level sets $X_d$ are open and closed. Quasi-compactness gives finitely many nonempty level sets: their open cover has a finite subcover. Each $f_d:X_d\to S$ is separated smooth of finite type of pure relative dimension $d$. Nagata compactification [thm-nagata-compactification] makes it compactifiable. Work on these finitely many pieces and take a common open of $S$ at the end; this is a decomposition of $X$, not of $S$.

Fix one piece and write $f$ for $f_d$. Put $\omega=f^\times\lambda_S$. By [thm-asd-smooth-tensor], $\omega=P[2d]$ with $P$ finite locally constant of rank one. Define $L^\vee=\mathcal Hom_\lambda(L,\lambda_X)$ and $N=L^\vee\otimes_\lambda P[2d]$. This ordinary tensor computes the derived tensor because the sheaves involved are locally finite free. On a trivializing etale neighborhood, $L=\lambda^r$ and $P=\lambda$, so $N=\lambda^r[2d]$ and the evaluation $L\to R\mathcal Hom_\lambda(N,\omega)$ is the bidual map $\lambda^r\to(\lambda^r)^\vee{}^\vee$, in degree zero. The internal Hom functor from $\lambda^r$ is a finite product of the identity and hence exact; there are no higher internal Ext terms. This computes an isomorphism locally, and the sheaf-level geometric-stalk criterion [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative], applied to cohomology, checks it globally. It also shows directly that $N$ is bounded constructible in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes]. Internal Hom here is the operation of [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] on the small etale ringed site, not a pro-etale or adic operation.

source.place: Proof, first paragraph: construction of N and evaluation

proof.text: Apply [prop-asd-internal-adjunction] with $M=N$ and $K=\lambda_S$. The evaluation identification from the preceding step gives a canonical isomorphism $\alpha_f:Rf_*L\xrightarrow{\sim}D_S(C)$, where $C=Rf_!N$ and $D_S(C)=R\mathcal Hom_\lambda(C,\lambda_S)$. By [lem-fin-compact-bounded-and-base-change], $C$ is bounded constructible. For each nonzero $\mathcal H^q(C)$ choose its finite locally closed stratification from [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes]. The stratum containing the generic point of integral $S$ contains an open neighborhood of that point: write its underlying set as $O\cap Z$, with $O$ open and $Z$ closed; since $Z$ contains the generic point, $Z=S$. Restrict to $O$. The finitely many degrees give a common nonempty open $U$. Include restriction to $U$ in the compact-support base-change clause of [lem-fin-compact-bounded-and-base-change], so that the same construction for $f_U$ has compact direct image $C|_U$. Apply [lem-fin-lisse-field-dual] to $C|_U$. Its cohomology formula makes $D_U(C|_U)$ bounded and finite locally constant, hence so is $Rf_{U,*}L|_{X_U}$ by $\alpha_{f_U}$. No ordinary direct-image finiteness theorem is used.

Let $v:T\to U$ have Noetherian source and let $v_X:X_T\to X_U$ be the other edge. The canonical comparison [prop-asd-smooth-base-change] identifies $v_X^*\omega_{f_U}$ with $\omega_{f_T}$ and respects the tensor map. Pulling back the finite-free evaluation of step 2 identifies $v_X^*N$ with $N_T=(v_X^*L)^\vee\otimes\omega_{f_T}$. This uses the identity $(\lambda^r)^\vee=\lambda^r$ on each trivializing neighborhood; pullback preserves that cover. Put $C_T=Rf_{T,!}N_T$. Compact-support exchange [lem-fin-compact-bounded-and-base-change] gives $b:v^*(C|_U)\xrightarrow{\sim}C_T$. The canonical dual-pullback map $a:v^*D_U(C|_U)\xrightarrow{\sim}D_T(v^*(C|_U))$ is an isomorphism by [lem-fin-lisse-field-dual]. Thus $D_T(b^{-1})\circ a$, together with $\alpha_{f_U}$ and $\alpha_{f_T}^{-1}$ from [prop-asd-internal-adjunction], gives an isomorphism $\beta:v^*Rf_{U,*}L\to Rf_{T,*}v_X^*L$. The adjunction for $f_T$ is available on its ambient Noetherian category even though $T$ need not be finite type over $k$: the base-changed compactification supplies compactifiability. More explicitly, [lem-pod-separated-finite-type-base-change] gives finite type of $f_T$, so [pqf-lem-locnoeth-lft] and quasi-compactness give Noetherian $X_T$. The chosen compactification base changes to a compactification by [lemma-nagata-compactification-base-change]. The prime $\ell$ stays invertible on $T$ because its inverse in $k$ pulls back along $T\to U\to\operatorname{Spec}k$.

Check the morphism, as follows. Let $B=Rf_{U,*}L$ and let $e:f_U^*B\to L$ be the ordinary counit. Use the canonical internal-adjunction isomorphism of [prop-asd-internal-adjunction], namely the map transposed from evaluation followed by the exceptional counit; $\alpha_{f_U}$ is obtained from the pairing $f_U^*B\otimes N\xrightarrow{e\otimes1}L\otimes N\xrightarrow{\mathrm{ev}}\omega_{f_U}$ and the exceptional counit $Rf_{U,!}\omega_{f_U}\to\lambda_U$. After pullback, the dual comparison $a$ is defined by pulling back this evaluation pairing. The map $D_T(b^{-1})$ substitutes $Rf_{T,!}N_T$ for $v^*Rf_{U,!}N$. The exceptional comparison [prop-asd-smooth-base-change] is the transpose of compact-support exchange followed by the pulled-back exceptional counit; consequently these two substitutions give precisely the pairing $f_T^*v^*B\otimes N_T\xrightarrow{v_X^*e\otimes1}v_X^*L\otimes N_T\xrightarrow{\mathrm{ev}}\omega_{f_T}$. Transpose back through the canonical internal adjunction over $T$. The ordinary-adjunction transpose of $\beta$ is therefore $f_T^*v^*B\cong v_X^*f_U^*B\xrightarrow{v_X^*e}v_X^*L$. This is exactly the inverse-image transpose defining the ordinary exchange in [sbc-def-base-change-map], on the square with its edges exchanged. Equality of transposes implies equality of maps. Hence the specified ordinary base-change morphism equals $\beta$ and is an isomorphism. In counit notation, if $c:v_X^*\omega_{f_U}\to\omega_{f_T}$ is the smooth comparison, its defining transpose says $\varepsilon_T\circ Rf_{T,!}(c)=v^*\varepsilon_U\circ b_{\omega}^{-1}$. For the pairing $p:f_U^*B\otimes N\to\omega_{f_U}$, naturality of compact exchange says $b_{\omega}\circ v^*Rf_{U,!}(p)=Rf_{T,!}(v_X^*p)\circ b_{f_U^*B\otimes N}$. Substituting the second equality in the first gives $\varepsilon_T Rf_{T,!}(c\circ v_X^*p)=v^*(\varepsilon_U Rf_{U,!}(p))\circ b_{f_U^*B\otimes N}^{-1}$, the equality of transposed pairings used above. These are identities of the defining evaluation and mate maps, so they require no additional finiteness or constructibility assertion.

source.place: Proof, last paragraph: identification of the canonical map

proof.text: Intersect the nonempty opens obtained for the finitely many $X_d$. They all contain the generic point, so their intersection $U$ is nonempty. A sheaf on a finite disjoint union is the tuple of its restrictions (the sheaf condition on the open-and-closed covering); sections over a base object are the finite product of sections on the pieces. Hence both direct-image constructions and their exchange maps are the finite products of those for $f_d$. Finite products are finite direct sums in an abelian category and are exact, so this equality persists upon deriving. Take the minimum and maximum of the finitely many cohomological bounds. Finite direct sums of finite locally constant sheaves are finite locally constant, as seen on a common trivializing etale cover. The component exchange maps are isomorphisms by step 5; their finite product is an isomorphism. If $X$ is empty the complex is zero and take $U=S$.
